term.definition: A line which a graph of a function approaches closely but never touches.
The function $$f(x) = \text{log}\ x$$ is the common logarithmic function with base$$10,$$ where $$x > 0.$$ $$y = \text{log}\ x\ \text{is equivalent to}\ x = 10^{y}$$
An exponential function, where $$a > 0$$ and $$a \neq 1,$$ is a function of the form $$f(x) = a^{x}.$$
The function $$f(x) = \text{log}_{a}x$$ is the logarithmic function with base $$a,$$ where $$a > 0,$$$$x > 0,$$ and $$a \neq 1.$$ $$y = \text{log}_{a}x\ \text{is equivalent to}\ x = a^{y}$$
The number e is defined as the value of $$\left( {1 + \frac{1}{n}} \right)^{n},$$ as n gets larger and larger. We say, as n increases without bound, $$e \approx 2.718281828...$$
The natural exponential function is an exponential function whose base is e: $$f(x) = e^{x}.$$ The domain is $$\left( {\text{−}\infty,\infty} \right)$$ and the range is $$\left( {0,\infty} \right).$$
The function $$f(x) = \text{ln}\ x$$ is the natural logarithmic function with base $$e,$$ where $$x > 0.$$ $$y = \text{ln}\ x\ \text{is equivalent to}\ x = e^{y}$$
A function is one-to-one if each value in the range has exactly one element in the domain. For each ordered pair in the function, each y-value is matched with only one x-value.
